items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the tax law, in relation to a tax credit for employers whose
employees utilize telecommuting and for necessary technology purchases made by
telecommuting employees; and providing for the repeal of such provisions upon
expiration thereof
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8248

SPONSOR: AVELLA
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the tax law, in relation to a tax
credit for employers whose employees utilize telecommuting and for
necessary technology purchases made by telecommuting employees; and
providing for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration thereof

 
PURPOSE:

This legislation would provide a tax credit for employers who allow
their employees to telecommute.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends Section 210-B of the tax law by adding new subdivision
53, which would provide for a tax credit for employers of qualified
resident telecommuting employees. In order for the employer to get cred-
it for an employee who telecommutes, that employee must be able to
perform a majority of the serves that are part of that employee's normal
workweek in the employee's residence in this state, without making any
work-related commute trips on the day or days that the employee is tele-
commuting.

Section 2 amends Section 606 of the tax law by adding new subsection
'ccc' that provides that employers can get a tax credit for telecommut-
ing employees from January 1, 2019 to January 1, 2021 equal to one
percent of the salary and wages paid by the employer during that period
to the qualifying employee, and provides for various definitions.

Section 3 amends subparagraph (B) of paragraph 1 of subection (1) of
section 606 of the tax law by adding new clause (xliv) which provides of
the inclusion of a tax credit for employers of telecommuting employees
under subsection 'ccc' of Section 606 of the tax law.

Section 4 further amends Section 606 of the tax law by adding a new
subsection 'kkk' which provides a five hundred dollar per year credit to
employee to purchase technology necessary to perform his or her job via
telecommuting.

Section 5 states that the act shall take effect immediately; provided,
however, that this act shall expire and be deemed repealed January 1,
2021; and provided, further, that this act shall apply to taxable years
commencing January 1, 2019.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Telecommuting, also known as teleworking, is an alternative work
arrangement in which an employee works outside of the standard office,
often from home. Studies have shown that there are various benefits for
both employers and employees when well-designed telecommuting programs
are established, including increased productivity, reduced turnover,
increased morale, and lower employer costs. Further, the federal govern-
ment, many states, and numerous municipalities have established tele-
working policies that have reduced carbon emissions and road congestion.

This legislation would create a tax credit to incentivize employers in
New York to enter into agreements with employees that authorize them to
telecommute. In addition, this legislation would provide a tax credit to
employees allowing them to purchase the technology necessary to perform
their jobs via telecommunication. After three years the tax credit would
be automatically repealed, unless further legislative action was taken,
giving employers and employees alike suitable time to observe the posi-
tive effects that telecommuting can have for both parties, and no longer
needing the tax incentive to maintain such programs.

By enacting this legislation, we can effectively incentivize employers
to explore the benefits of telecommuting and make New York both a more
business and worker friendly state.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately, with provisions.

summary: Establishes that there shall be a tax credit in an amount equal to one percent of the salary and wages paid by an employer to a qualified residential telecommuting employee residing in the state, and a tax credit of up to five hundred dollars a year for necessary technology purchases of telecommuting employees.
title: Relates to providing a tax credit for employers of employees who telecommute and for necessary technology purchases of telecommuting employees
